relationships.description: The equivalence or boundary class is an integral part of exactly one input space partition and has no existence once that partition of the input field's domain is removed.
relationships.evidence: The test-design model file lists the partition value nested under the input space partition's values collection, and the value carries no identity outside that parent.

relationships.description: The coverage criterion, such as boundary-values or pairwise, determines whether and in what combinations this equivalence class must be exercised by the target's test cases.
relationships.evidence: The coverage requirement's definition names the partition value, or its parent partition, among the selected input partitions it must cover.

relationships.description: The equivalence class is meaningful only under a particular environmental condition, such as a locale or dependency version, because that condition determines which values fall into the class or behave alike.
relationships.evidence: The partition value's boundary condition or representative value is stated relative to a named environment factor, for example a locale-specific date format or a value limit tied to an OS version.

relationships.description: Inputs drawn from this equivalence class are expected to produce results of the named outcome category, such as a validation error for an out-of-range boundary class.
relationships.evidence: The test design maps the partition value to an expected outcome category, or test case sketches that use its representative value are grouped under that category.

relationships.description: The equivalence class points to a signed-off exclusion decision that explains why tests are not required to exercise it.
relationships.evidence: The partition value record carries an exclusion identifier that matches an approved coverage exclusion entry with its rationale and approver.

relationships.description: A required equivalence class that no implemented or executed test exercises gives rise to a recorded coverage gap finding.
relationships.evidence: A coverage gap record names the partition value, or its representative value, as the uncovered element, and coverage analysis output shows no test case using it.

notes: The references link to CoverageExclusion is questionable. Exclusions are defined as applying to coverage targets or requirements, not partition values. Triggers to CoverageGap is also loose: gaps are defined against requirements or targets, and an analysis process rather than the value itself produces them. The depends-on link to EnvironmentFactor mixes input-space and environment concerns that the definitions keep separate.
